p2.original: Information Overload in the Information Age

p3.original: To post or not to post? Every day we are faced with a myriad of decisions, from what to have for breakfast, to which show to stream, to the more complex—“Should I double major and add possibly another semester of study to my education?” Our response to these choices depends on the information we have available at any given moment. Economists call this “imperfect” because we rarely have all the data we need to make perfect decisions. Despite the lack of perfect information, we still make hundreds of decisions a day.

p15.original: What Is Economics, and Why Is It Important?
p15.zh: 什么是经济学,为什么它很重要?

p16.original: Economics is the study of how humans make decisions in the face of scarcity. These can be individual decisions, family decisions, business decisions or societal decisions. If you look around carefully, you will see that scarcity is a fact of life. Scarcity means that human wants for goods, services and resources exceed what is available. Resources, such as labor, tools, land, and raw materials are necessary to produce the goods and services we want but they exist in limited supply. Of course, the ultimate scarce resource is time- everyone, rich or poor, has just 24 expendable hours in the day to earn income to acquire goods and services, for leisure time, or for sleep. At any point in time, there is only a finite amount of resources available.
p16.zh: 经济学是研究人类在稀缺情况下如何决策. 这些可以是个人决定、家庭决定、商业决定或社会决定。 如果你仔细看看,你会看到 缺乏是生活的事实。匮乏意味着人类对货物、服务和资源的渴望超过了现有水平。劳动力、工具、土地和原材料等资源是生产我们想要的货物和服务的必要条件,但它们的供应有限。 当然,最终的稀缺资源是时间,无论贫富,每个人白天只有24个消耗性小时来赚取收入,以获得商品和服务,休闲时间,或睡眠时间. 在任何时间,可动用的资源都有限。

p17.original: Think about it this way: In 2015 the labor force in the United States contained over 158 million workers, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The total land area was 3,794,101 square miles. While these are certainly large numbers, they are not infinite. Because these resources are limited, so are the numbers of goods and services we produce with them. Combine this with the fact that human wants seem to be virtually infinite, and you can see why scarcity is a problem.
p17.zh: 如此思考:2015年,美国劳动力中包含超过1.58亿工人,据美国称.劳动统计局.土地总面积为3,794,101平方英里. 虽然这些数目确实很多,但并非无限。因为这些资源有限,我们与之共同生产的货物和服务数量也有限。 把这一点与人类想要的几乎是无限的这一事实结合起来, 你可以明白为什么稀缺是一个问题。

p30.original: If you still do not believe that scarcity is a problem, consider the following: Does everyone require food to eat? Does everyone need a decent place to live? Does everyone have access to healthcare? In every country in the world, there are people who are hungry, homeless (for example, those who call park benches their beds, as  shows), and in need of healthcare, just to focus on a few critical goods and services. Why is this the case? It is because of scarcity. Let’s delve into the concept of scarcity a little deeper, because it is crucial to understanding economics.
p30.zh: 如果你仍然不认为稀缺是一个问题,请考虑以下几点: 每个人都需要食物吃吗? 每个人都需要一个体面的住处吗? 每个人都有机会获得医疗保健吗?在世界每一个国家,都有饥饿、无家可归的人(例如,有人叫公园的长椅上铺床)和需要医疗保健的人,他们只注重一些关键的商品和服务。 为什么这样?这是因为缺乏资源。 让我们更深入地探讨稀缺的概念,因为它对理解经济学至关重要。

p32.original: Think about all the things you consume: food, shelter, clothing, transportation, healthcare, and entertainment. How do you acquire those items? You do not produce them yourself. You buy them. How do you afford the things you buy? You work for pay. If you do not, someone else does on your behalf. Yet most of us never have enough income to buy all the things we want. This is because of scarcity. So how do we solve it?
p32.zh: 想想你消费的所有东西:食物、住所、衣服、交通、保健和娱乐。 你怎么买这些东西的? 你没有自己生产它们。 你买的 你怎么买得起你买的东西? 你为薪水工作。 如果你不这样做,别人会为你做。 然而,我们大多数人的收入永远不足以购买我们想要的一切。这是因为缺乏资源。 那么,我们如何解决它呢?

p34.original: Every society, at every level, must make choices about how to use its resources. Families must decide whether to spend their money on a new car or a fancy vacation. Towns must choose whether to put more of the budget into police and fire protection or into the school system. Nations must decide whether to devote more funds to national defense or to protecting the environment. In most cases, there just isn’t enough money in the budget to do everything.  How do we use our limited resources the best way possible, that is, to obtain the most goods and services we can?  There are a couple of options.  First, we could each produce everything we each consume.  Alternatively, we could each produce some of what we want to consume, and “trade” for the rest of what we want.  Let’s explore these options. Why do we not each just produce all of the things we consume? Think back to pioneer days, when individuals knew how to do so much more than we do today, from building their homes, to growing their crops, to hunting for food, to repairing their equipment. Most of us do not know how to do all—or any—of those things, but it is not because we could not learn. Rather, we do not have to. The reason why is something called the division and specialization of labor, a production innovation first put forth by Adam Smith () in his book, The Wealth of Nations.
p34.zh: 每一个社会,在各个层面,都必须就如何使用其资源作出选择。家庭必须决定是把钱花在一辆新车上,还是花花样的假期上.城镇必须选择是将更多的预算投入警察和消防工作,还是投入学校系统。国家必须决定是否将更多资金用于国防或保护环境。多数情况下, 预算中没有足够的钱来做一切。 我们如何利用我们有限的资源,即尽可能最佳地获得我们所能获得的货物和服务?有几个选择。 首先,我们每个人都可以生产我们消耗的一切。 或者,我们每个人都可以生产一些我们想要消费的东西,并且“贸易”来换取我们想要的其余东西。 让我们探讨这些选择。 为什么我们不各自生产 我们消费的所有东西? 回想一下先锋时代,当人们知道如何比我们今天做得多得多的时候,从建造家园,到种植庄稼,到打猎觅食,到修理设备. 我们大多数人不知道如何做所有这些事情,但这并不是因为我们无法学习。 相反,我们不必这样做。原因就是所谓的劳动分工和专业化,这是亚当·斯密(英语:Adam Smith ())在他的著作"国家财富"中首次提出的生产创新.

p36.original: The Division of and Specialization of Labor

p37.original: The formal study of economics began when Adam Smith (1723–1790) published his famous book The Wealth of Nations in 1776. Many authors had written on economics in the centuries before Smith, but he was the first to address the subject in a comprehensive way. In the first chapter, Smith introduces the concept of division of labor, which means that the way one produces a good or service is divided into a number of tasks that different workers perform, instead of all the tasks being done by the same person.
p37.zh: 正式的经济学研究始于亚当·斯密(1723–1790)于1776年出版他的著名著作"国家财富". 在史密斯之前的几个世纪中,许多作者都曾写过经济学著作,但他是第一个以全面的方式论述这个主题的. 在第一章中,史密斯引入了分工的概念,这意味着一个人生产一种商品或服务的方式被分为一些不同工人完成的任务,而不是由同一人完成的所有任务.

p38.original: To illustrate division of labor, Smith counted how many tasks went into making a pin: drawing out a piece of wire, cutting it to the right length, straightening it, putting a head on one end and a point on the other, and packaging pins for sale, to name just a few. Smith counted 18 distinct tasks that different people performed—all for a pin, believe it or not!
p38.zh: 为了说明劳动分工,史密斯计算出制造一个针头的工夫:拔出一根线条,切到合适的长度,理直气壮,把头放在一端和另一端一个点,包装针头出售,仅举几个例子.Smith统计了不同人所完成的18项不同的任务——都是为了一个针,信不信由你!

p39.original: Modern businesses divide tasks as well. Even a relatively simple business like a restaurant divides the task of serving meals into a range of jobs like top chef, sous chefs, less-skilled kitchen help, servers to wait on the tables, a greeter at the door, janitors to clean up, and a business manager to handle paychecks and bills—not to mention the economic connections a restaurant has with suppliers of food, furniture, kitchen equipment, and the building where it is located. A complex business like a large manufacturing factory, such as the shoe factory (), or a hospital can have hundreds of job classifications.
p39.zh: 现代企业也分担任务。 甚至像餐厅这样的相对简单的企业,把提供膳食的任务分成一系列的工作,如顶级厨师、Sous厨师、技能较低的厨房帮手、在餐桌上等待的服务器、门口的问候器、清洁工、以及处理工资和账单的商业经理——更不用提一家餐馆与食品、家具、厨房设备供应商及其所在大楼的经济联系。类似大型制造厂,如鞋厂(),或医院等复杂的企业可以拥有数百个工作分类.

p41.original: Why the Division of Labor Increases Production
p41.zh: 劳动分工为什么增加生产

p42.original: When we divide and subdivide the tasks involved with producing a good or service, workers and businesses can produce a greater quantity of output. In his observations of pin factories, Smith noticed that one worker alone might make 20 pins in a day, but that a small business of 10 workers (some of whom would need to complete two or three of the 18 tasks involved with pin-making), could make 48,000 pins in a day. How can a group of workers, each specializing in certain tasks, produce so much more than the same number of workers who try to produce the entire good or service by themselves? Smith offered three reasons.
p42.zh: 当我们划分和细分生产商品或服务的任务时,工人和企业可以产生更多的产出。史密斯在对披针工厂的观察中注意到,一个工人单独一天可能做20个披针,但一个由10个工人组成的小企业(其中一些工人需要完成与披针制造有关的18项任务中的两到三个),一天可以做48000个披针.一群专门从事某些工作的工人,怎么能够生产出这么多的工人,他们自己去生产全部的好品或服务呢?史密斯提出了三个原因.

p43.original: First, specialization in a particular small job allows workers to focus on the parts of the production process where they have an advantage. (In later chapters, we will develop this idea by discussing comparative advantage.) People have different skills, talents, and interests, so they will be better at some jobs than at others. The particular advantages may be based on educational choices, which are in turn shaped by interests and talents. Only those with medical degrees qualify to become doctors, for instance. For some goods, geography affects specialization. For example, it is easier to be a wheat farmer in North Dakota than in Florida, but easier to run a tourist hotel in Florida than in North Dakota. If you live in or near a big city, it is easier to attract enough customers to operate a successful dry cleaning business or movie theater than if you live in a sparsely populated rural area. Whatever the reason, if people specialize in the production of what they do best, they will be more effective than if they produce a combination of things, some of which they are good at and some of which they are not.
p43.zh: 第一,在某一个小工作方面实现专业化,使工人能够集中精力从事他们有优势的生产过程。(在后面的章节中,我们将通过讨论比较优势来发展这个想法. )人们拥有不同的技能,才智和兴趣,因此他们在某些工作上会比其他工作更好.特殊的好处可能基于教育选择,而教育选择又由兴趣和才能决定。 例如,只有具有医学学位的人才有资格成为医生。 对于一些商品来说,地理影响专业化。 例如,在北达科他州做小麦农比在佛罗里达州更容易,但在佛罗里达州经营一家旅游酒店比在北达科他州更容易. 如果住在大城市或附近,比住在人口稀少的农村地区更容易吸引足够的顾客经营成功的干洗业或电影院. 无论什么原因,如果人们专门从事自己最擅长的制作,那么他们比他们制作各种事物的组合,有些是他们擅长的,有些是他们不擅长的,那么他们的效果就会更好.

p44.original: Second, workers who specialize in certain tasks often learn to produce more quickly and with higher quality. This pattern holds true for many workers, including assembly line laborers who build cars, stylists who cut hair, and doctors who perform heart surgery. In fact, specialized workers often know their jobs well enough to suggest innovative ways to do their work faster and better.
p44.zh: 第二,专门从事某些工作的工人往往学会更快、更高质量的生产。 这种模式对许多工人都是如此,包括装配线工人制造汽车,剪发的造型师,以及做心脏手术的医生. 事实上,专业工人往往对自己的工作十分了解,足以提出创新办法,加快和更好地开展工作。

p45.original: A similar pattern often operates within businesses. In many cases, a business that focuses on one or a few products (sometimes called its “core competency”) is more successful than firms that try to make a wide range of products.
p45.zh: 类似模式往往在企业中运作。在许多情况下,一个侧重于一种或几种产品(有时称为“核心能力”)的企业比那些试图制造多种产品的公司更成功。

p46.original: Third, specialization allows businesses to take advantage of economies of scale, which means that for many goods, as the level of production increases, the average cost of producing each individual unit declines. For example, if a factory produces only 100 cars per year, each car will be quite expensive to make on average. However, if a factory produces 50,000 cars each year, then it can set up an assembly line with huge machines and workers performing specialized tasks, and the average cost of production per car will be lower. The ultimate result of workers who can focus on their preferences and talents, learn to do their specialized jobs better, and work in larger organizations is that society as a whole can produce and consume far more than if each person tried to produce all of their own goods and services. The division and specialization of labor has been a force against the problem of scarcity.
p46.zh: 第三,专业化使企业能够利用规模经济,这意味着对于许多商品,随着生产水平的提高,每个单位生产的平均成本下降. 例如,如果一家工厂每年只生产100辆汽车,那么每辆汽车平均造价会相当昂贵. 然而,如果一个工厂每年生产5万辆汽车,那么它就可以搭建一条装有巨大机器和从事专门任务的工人的装配线,每辆汽车的平均生产成本将会降低.工人能够专注于他们的喜好和才智,学会更好地完成他们专门的工作,并在更大的组织中工作,其最终结果是,整个社会能够生产和消费远远超出每个人试图生产他们自己所有商品和服务的程度。劳动力的分工和专业化一直是解决稀缺问题的力量。

p48.original: Specialization only makes sense, though, if workers can use the pay they receive for doing their jobs to purchase the other goods and services that they need. In short, specialization requires trade.
p48.zh: 但是,如果工人能够利用工作所得的工资购买他们需要的其他货物和服务,专业化才有意义。简言之,专业化需要贸易。

p49.original: You do not have to know anything about electronics or sound systems to play music—you just buy an iPod or MP3 player, download the music, and listen. You do not have to know anything about artificial fibers or the construction of sewing machines if you need a jacket—you just buy the jacket and wear it. You do not need to know anything about internal combustion engines to operate a car—you just get in and drive. Instead of trying to acquire all the knowledge and skills involved in producing all of the goods and services that you wish to consume, the market allows you to learn a specialized set of skills and then use the pay you receive to buy the goods and services you need or want. This is how our modern society has evolved into a strong economy.
p49.zh: 你不需要知道任何关于电子或音响系统的知识就可以播放音乐——你只需要买一个iPod或MP3播放器,下载音乐,并听. 你不需要了解人工纤维或缝纫机的构造,如果你需要一件夹克的话——你只要买下夹克,就穿它。 你不需要知道任何关于内燃机操作汽车的知识,市场不但没有试图获得生产所有你想要消费的商品和服务所涉及的所有知识和技能,反而允许你学习一套专门的技能,然后用你得到的薪水购买你需要或想要的商品和服务. 这就是我们现代社会如何演变成一个强大的经济.

p51.original: Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, and Michael Kremer
p51.zh: 埃斯特·杜弗洛、阿比吉特·巴内尔吉和迈克尔·克雷默

p52.original: Now that you have an overview on what economics studies, let’s quickly discuss why you are right to study it. Economics is not primarily a collection of facts to memorize, although there are plenty of important concepts to learn. Instead, think of economics as a collection of questions to answer or puzzles to work. Most importantly, economics provides the tools to solve those puzzles.
p52.zh: 现在,你对经济学研究有一个总的看法,让我们快速讨论一下为什么你研究它是正确的。经济学主要不是要记住的事实集合,尽管有许多重要的概念需要学习. 相反,将经济学视为一个问题集,用来回答问题或解谜来工作.最重要的是,经济学提供了解决这些谜题的工具。

p53.original: Consider the complex and critical issue of education barriers on national and regional levels, which affect millions of people and result in widespread poverty and inequality. Governments, aid organizations, and wealthy individuals spend billions of dollars each year trying to address these issues. Nations announce the revitalization of their education programs; tech companies donate devices and infrastructure, and celebrities and charities build schools and sponsor students. Yet the problems remain, sometimes almost as pronounced as they were before the intervention. Why is that the case? In 2019, three economists—Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, and Michael Kremer—were awarded the Nobel Prize for their work to answer those questions. They worked diligently to break the widespread problems into smaller pieces, and experimented with small interventions to test success. The award citation credited their work with giving the world better tools and information to address poverty and improve education. Esther Duflo, who is the youngest person and second woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics, said, "We believed that like the war on cancer, the war on poverty was not going to be won in one major battle, but in a series of small triumphs. . . . This work and the culture of learning that it fostered in governments has led to real improvement in the lives of hundreds of millions of poor people.”
p53.zh: 考虑国家和区域两级的教育障碍这一复杂和关键问题,这些障碍影响到数百万人,并造成普遍的贫穷和不平等。 政府、援助组织和富人每年花费数十亿美元来解决这些问题。国家宣布振兴其教育方案;技术公司捐赠设备和基础设施,名人和慈善机构建造学校和赞助学生。 然而,问题依然存在,有时与干预前的问题几乎相同。 为什么?2019年,三位经济学家——埃瑟·杜弗洛(Esther Duflo),阿比吉特·巴内尔吉(Abhijit Banerjee),迈克尔·克雷默(Michael Kremer)——因回答这些问题而获得诺贝尔奖. 他们勤奋工作,把广泛的问题打碎成小块,用小的干预来试验成功.获奖者赞扬他们为世界提供更好的工具和信息,以解决贫困和改善教育问题。以斯帖·杜弗洛(Esther Duflo)是获得诺贝尔经济学奖的最小的人和第二位女性,他说:"我们相信,像癌症战争一样,在一场大战中,消除贫困的战争不会胜利,而是在一系列小胜利中获胜. .这项工作及其在政府中培养的学习文化使数亿穷人的生活得到真正的改善。”

p54.original: As you can see, economics affects far more than business. For example:
p54.zh: 如你所见,经济影响远大于商业影响. 例如:

p55.original: Virtually every major problem facing the world today, from global warming, to world poverty, to the conflicts in Syria, Afghanistan, and Somalia, has an economic dimension. If you are going to be part of solving those problems, you need to be able to understand them. Economics is crucial.
p55.zh: 当今世界面临的几乎所有重大问题,从全球变暖到世界贫困,到叙利亚、阿富汗和索马里的冲突,都具有经济层面。 如果你要参与解决这些问题,你就必须能够理解这些问题。经济学至关重要。

p56.original: It is hard to overstate the importance of economics to good citizenship. You need to be able to vote intelligently on budgets, regulations, and laws in general. When the U.S. government came close to a standstill at the end of 2012 due to the “fiscal cliff,” what were the issues? Did you know?
p56.zh: 经济学对良好公民的重要性怎么强调都不过分。需要能够明智地对预算,法规,以及一般法律进行投票. 当美国政府在2012年底因“财政悬崖”而陷入僵局时, 你知道吗?

p57.original: A basic understanding of economics makes you a well-rounded thinker. When you read articles about economic issues, you will understand and be able to evaluate the writer’s argument. When you hear classmates, co-workers, or political candidates talking about economics, you will be able to distinguish between common sense and nonsense. You will find new ways of thinking about current events and about personal and business decisions, as well as current events and politics.
p57.zh: 对经济学的基本理解,使你成为一个周密的思想家. 当你阅读有关经济问题的文章时,你会理解并能够评价作家的论点。 当你听到同学,同事,或政治候选人谈论经济学时,你就能区分常识和胡说八道. 你会找到新的思维方式,思考时事,个人和企业决策,以及时事和政治.

p58.original: The study of economics does not dictate the answers, but it can illuminate the different choices.
p58.zh: 对经济学的研究并不决定答案,但它可以阐明不同的选择。

p60.original: Economics seeks to solve the problem of scarcity, which is when human wants for goods and services exceed the available supply. A modern economy displays a division of labor, in which people earn income by specializing in what they produce and then use that income to purchase the products they need or want. The division of labor allows individuals and firms to specialize and to produce more for several reasons: a) It allows the agents to focus on areas of advantage due to natural factors and skill levels; b) It encourages the agents to learn and invent; c) It allows agents to take advantage of economies of scale. Division and specialization of labor only work when individuals can purchase what they do not produce in markets. Learning about economics helps you understand the major problems facing the world today, prepares you to be a good citizen, and helps you become a well-rounded thinker.
p60.zh: 经济学寻求解决稀缺问题,即人类对货物和服务的需求超过现有供应。现代经济呈现出分工,人们通过专门生产什么来赚取收入,然后利用这种收入购买他们需要或想要的产品.劳动分工允许个人和公司专门化生产,原因有几方面:(a) 它允许代理人专注于自然因素和技能水平造成的优势领域;(b) 它鼓励代理人学习和发明;(c) 它允许代理人利用规模经济。只有在个人能够购买他们不在市场上生产的东西时,劳动分工和专业化才能发挥作用。学习经济学有助于你理解当今世界所面临的重大问题,让你做好成为好公民的准备,帮助你成为一个全方位的思想家.

p62.original: What is scarcity? Can you think of two causes of scarcity?
p62.zh: 什么是稀缺? 你能想到缺血的两个原因吗?

p63.original: Scarcity means human wants for goods and services exceed the available supply. Supply is limited because resources are limited. Demand, however, is virtually unlimited. Whatever the supply, it seems human nature to want more.
p63.zh: 稀缺意味着人类对商品和服务的需求超过现有供应.供应有限,因为资源有限。 然而,需求几乎是无限的。 无论供应多少,似乎人类本性需要更多的.

p64.original: Residents of the town of Smithfield like to consume hams, but each ham requires 10 people to produce it and takes a month. If the town has a total of 100 people, what is the maximum amount of ham the residents can consume in a month?
p64.zh: 史密斯菲尔德镇的居民喜欢吃火腿,但每个火腿需要10人生产,需要一个月. 如果全镇共有100人,那么居民一个月内能消耗的火腿最多多少?.

p65.original: 100 people / 10 people per ham = a maximum of 10 hams per month if all residents produce ham. Since consumption is limited by production, the maximum number of hams residents could consume per month is 10.
p65.zh: 100人/每火腿10人 = 如果所有居民都生产火腿,每月最多10个火腿. 由于消费受生产限制,每月可消费的火腿居民最多可达10人.

p66.original: A consultant works for $200 per hour. She likes to eat vegetables, but is not very good at growing them. Why does it make more economic sense for her to spend her time at the consulting job and shop for her vegetables?
p66.zh: 一名顾问每小时工作200美元。 她喜欢吃蔬菜,但不太擅长种植蔬菜. 为什么她花时间做咨询工作,买菜,这在经济上更有意义?

p67.original: She is very productive at her consulting job, but not very productive growing vegetables. Time spent consulting would produce far more income than it what she could save growing her vegetables using the same amount of time. So on purely economic grounds, it makes more sense for her to maximize her income by applying her labor to what she does best (i.e. specialization of labor).
p67.zh: 她的咨询工作非常有生产力,但种植蔬菜的工作却不太有生产力。花在咨询上的时间将产生比她用同样时间节省的蔬菜收入多得多的收入。 因此,在纯粹的经济基础上,她通过将自己的劳动应用到她最擅长的工作(即劳动专业化)中来实现收入最大化更有意义.

p68.original: A computer systems engineer could paint her house, but it makes more sense for her to hire a painter to do it. Explain why.
p68.zh: 一个计算机系统工程师可以画她的房子,但是她雇一个画家来做这个更合理.解释为什么。

p69.original: The engineer is better at computer science than at painting. Thus, his time is better spent working for pay at his job and paying a painter to paint his house. Of course, this assumes he does not paint his house for fun!
p69.zh: 工程师在计算机科学方面比在绘画方面要好. 因此,他的时间最好花在工作上挣钱,并付钱给画家画他的房子. 当然,这假设他不 画他的房子为乐趣!

p71.original: Give the three reasons that explain why the division of labor increases an economy’s level of production.
p71.zh: 给出三个原因来解释为什么劳动分工会提高经济的生产水平.

p72.original: What are three reasons to study economics?
p72.zh: 研究经济学有三个理由?

p74.original: Suppose you have a team of two workers: one is a baker and one is a chef. Explain why the kitchen can produce more meals in a given period of time if each worker specializes in what they do best than if each worker tries to do everything from appetizer to dessert.
p74.zh: 假设你们有两组工人:一个是面包师,一个是厨师.解释一下,如果每个工人都专门从事他们最擅长的工作,那么为什么厨房可以在一定的时间内生产更多的饭菜,而不是如果每个工人都试图做从开胃菜到甜点的一切事情.

p75.original: Why would division of labor without trade not work?
p75.zh: 为什么没有贸易的分工是行不通的?

p76.original: Can you think of any examples of free goods, that is, goods or services that are not scarce?
p76.zh: 你能想到任何免费商品的例子, 即不稀缺的商品或服务吗?

p80.zh: 微观经济学和宏观经济学

p81.original: Economics is concerned with the well-being of all people, including those with jobs and those without jobs, as well as those with high incomes and those with low incomes. Economics acknowledges that production of useful goods and services can create problems of environmental pollution. It explores the question of how investing in education helps to develop workers’ skills. It probes questions like how to tell when big businesses or big labor unions are operating in a way that benefits society as a whole and when they are operating in a way that benefits their owners or members at the expense of others. It looks at how government spending, taxes, and regulations affect decisions about production and consumption.
p81.zh: 经济学关注所有人的福祉,包括有工作的人和没有工作的人,以及高收入的人和低收入的人。经济学承认,生产有用的货物和服务可造成环境污染问题。 它探讨了教育投资如何有助于发展工人技能的问题。 它调查的问题包括:如何确定大企业或大工会何时以有利于整个社会的方式运作,以及何时以牺牲他人的利益的方式运作,使其所有人或成员受益。 它研究了政府开支、税收和条例如何影响有关生产和消费的决定。

p82.original: It should be clear by now that economics covers considerable ground. We can divide that ground into two parts: Microeconomics focuses on the actions of individual agents within the economy, like households, workers, and businesses. Macroeconomics looks at the economy as a whole. It focuses on broad issues such as growth of production, the number of unemployed people, the inflationary increase in prices, government deficits, and levels of exports and imports. Microeconomics and macroeconomics are not separate subjects, but rather complementary perspectives on the overall subject of the economy.
p82.zh: 现在应该很清楚的是,经济学覆盖了相当大的基础。 我们可以将这一方面分为两个部分:微观经济学侧重于经济中个体代理人的行动,如家庭、工人和企业。宏观经济学从整体上看经济. 它侧重于广泛的问题,如生产增长、失业人数、价格上涨、政府赤字以及进出口水平。微观经济学和宏观经济学并不是独立的主体,而是对经济整体主体的互补视角.

p83.original: To understand why both microeconomic and macroeconomic perspectives are useful, consider the problem of studying a biological ecosystem like a lake. One person who sets out to study the lake might focus on specific topics: certain kinds of algae or plant life; the characteristics of particular fish or snails; or the trees surrounding the lake. Another person might take an overall view and instead consider the lake's ecosystem from top to bottom; what eats what, how the system stays in a rough balance, and what environmental stresses affect this balance. Both approaches are useful, and both examine the same lake, but the viewpoints are different. In a similar way, both microeconomics and macroeconomics study the same economy, but each has a different viewpoint.
p83.zh: 要了解微观经济和宏观经济观点为何有用,就考虑研究像湖泊一样的生物生态系统的问题。 一个开始研究湖的人可能侧重于特定主题:某些种类的藻类或植物生物;特定鱼类或蜗牛的特征;或湖泊周围的树木. 另一个人可能从整体上看,而是考虑湖的生态系统从上到下;什么是吃什么,系统如何保持粗糙的平衡,什么是环境压力影响这种平衡.这两种方法都是有益的,两者都考察同一个湖,但观点不同. 同样,微观经济学和宏观经济学都研究同一经济体,但每种方法都有不同的观点。

p84.original: Whether you are scrutinizing lakes or economics, the micro and the macro insights should blend with each other. In studying a lake, the micro insights about particular plants and animals help to understand the overall food chain, while the macro insights about the overall food chain help to explain the environment in which individual plants and animals live.
p84.zh: 无论你们在考察湖泊还是经济,微观和宏观的洞察力应该相互融合。 在研究一个湖泊时,对特定动植物的微观洞察有助于了解整个食物链,而对于整个食物链的宏观洞察有助于解释单个植物和动物所生活的环境.

p85.original: In economics, the micro decisions of individual businesses are influenced by whether the macroeconomy is healthy. For example, firms will be more likely to hire workers if the overall economy is growing. In turn, macroeconomy's performance ultimately depends on the microeconomic decisions that individual households and businesses make.
p85.zh: 在经济学中,个体企业的微观决策受宏观经济是否健康的影响. 例如,如果整个经济正在增长,公司就更有可能雇用工人。反过来,宏观经济的表现最终取决于个别家庭和企业作出的微观经济决定。

p87.original: What determines how households and individuals spend their budgets? What combination of goods and services will best fit their needs and wants, given the budget they have to spend? How do people decide whether to work, and if so, whether to work full time or part time? How do people decide how much to save for the future, or whether they should borrow to spend beyond their current means?
p87.zh: 是什么决定了家庭和个人如何使用其预算? 鉴于他们必须花费的预算,哪些商品和服务组合最适合他们的需要和愿望? 人们如何决定是工作,如果是,是全职还是兼职? 人们如何决定为未来存多少,还是应该借钱,以超出他们目前的能力?

p88.original: What determines the products, and how many of each, a firm will produce and sell? What determines the prices a firm will charge? What determines how a firm will produce its products? What determines how many workers it will hire? How will a firm finance its business? When will a firm decide to expand, downsize, or even close? In the microeconomics part of this book, we will learn about the theory of consumer behavior, the theory of the firm, how markets for labor and other resources work, and how markets sometimes fail to work properly.
p88.zh: 由什么决定产品,以及每家公司中有多少公司将生产和销售?公司要收取的价格由什么决定?公司如何生产产品,由什么决定?是什么决定了它将雇用多少工人?企业如何为企业融资?企业何时决定扩张,缩小规模,甚至关闭? 在这本书的微观经济学部分,我们将学习消费者行为理论,公司理论,劳动力和其他资源市场如何运作,以及市场有时如何不能正常运作.

p90.original: What determines the level of economic activity in a society? In other words, what determines how many goods and services a nation actually produces? What determines how many jobs are available in an economy? What determines a nation’s standard of living? What causes the economy to speed up or slow down? What causes firms to hire more workers or to lay them off? Finally, what causes the economy to grow over the long term?
p90.zh: 是什么决定了一个社会的经济活动水平?换句话说,什么决定了一个国家实际生产多少货物和服务?经济中有多少工作?一个国家的生活水平是怎样决定的呢?是什么导致经济加速或放慢?是什么导致公司雇用更多的工人或解雇他们? 最后,是什么因素导致经济长期增长?

p91.original: We can determine an economy's macroeconomic health by examining a number of goals: growth in the standard of living, low unemployment, and low inflation, to name the most important. How can we use government macroeconomic policy to pursue these goals? A nation's central bank conducts monetary policy, which involves policies that affect bank lending, interest rates, and financial capital markets. For the United States, this is the Federal Reserve. A nation's legislative body determines fiscal policy, which involves government spending and taxes. For the United States, this is the Congress and the executive branch, which originates the federal budget. These are the government's main tools. Americans tend to expect that government can fix whatever economic problems we encounter, but to what extent is that expectation realistic? These are just some of the issues that we will explore in the macroeconomic chapters of this book.
p91.zh: 我们可以通过审查一些目标来确定一个经济体的宏观经济健康:生活水平的增长、低失业率和低通货膨胀,这最要紧。 我们如何利用政府的宏观经济政策来实现这些目标?一个国家的中央银行实行货币政策,这涉及影响银行贷款、利率和金融资本市场的政策。 对于美国来说,这是联邦储备。一个国家的立法机构决定财政政策,这涉及政府开支和税收。 对于美国来说,这是国会和行政部门,它们来源于联邦预算. 这些是政府的主要工具.美国人倾向于期望政府能够解决我们遇到的任何经济问题,但这种期望在多大程度上是现实的? 这些只是我们将在本书的宏观经济章节中探讨的一些问题。

p93.original: Microeconomics and macroeconomics are two different perspectives on the economy. The microeconomic perspective focuses on parts of the economy: individuals, firms, and industries. The macroeconomic perspective looks at the economy as a whole, focusing on goals like growth in the standard of living, unemployment, and inflation. Macroeconomics has two types of policies for pursuing these goals: monetary policy and fiscal policy.
p93.zh: 微观经济学和宏观经济学是经济的两个不同视角.微观经济观点侧重于经济的几个部分:个人、公司和工业。宏观经济观点从整体上审视整个经济,侧重于生活水平增长、失业和通货膨胀等目标。宏观经济有两种政策来实现这些目标:货币政策和财政政策。

p95.original: What would be another example of a “system” in the real world that could serve as a metaphor for micro and macroeconomics?
p95.zh: 现实世界中的“体系”可以作为微观和宏观经济的比喻的另一个例子是什么?

p96.original: There are many physical systems that would work, for example, the study of planets (micro) in the solar system (macro), or solar systems (micro) in the galaxy (macro).
p96.zh: 有许多物理系统可以发挥作用,例如研究太阳系(宏观)中的行星(微),或研究银河系(宏观)中的太阳系(微).

p98.original: What is the difference between microeconomics and macroeconomics?
p98.zh: 微观经济学与宏观经济学有何区别?

p99.original: What are examples of individual economic agents?
p99.zh: 个人经济行为主体的例子是什么?

p100.original: What are the three main goals of macroeconomics?
p100.zh: 宏观经济的三个主要目标是什么?

p102.original: A balanced federal budget and a balance of trade are secondary goals of macroeconomics, while growth in the standard of living (for example) is a primary goal. Why do you think that is so?
p102.zh: 平衡的联邦预算和贸易平衡是宏观经济的次要目标,而生活水平的增长(例如)是首要目标。为何如此?

p103.original: Macroeconomics is an aggregate of what happens at the microeconomic level. Would it be possible for what happens at the macro level to differ from how economic agents would react to some stimulus at the micro level? Hint: Think about the behavior of crowds.
p103.zh: 宏观经济学是微观经济层面发生的情况的总和.宏观层面发生的情况与经济行为主体如何对微观层面的某些刺激作出反应有区别吗?提示:想一想群众的行为.

p104.original: How Economists Use Theories and Models to Understand Economic Issues
p104.zh: 经济学家如何利用理论和模型来理解经济问题

p106.original: John Maynard Keynes (1883–1946), one of the greatest economists of the twentieth century, pointed out that economics is not just a subject area but also a way of thinking. Keynes () famously wrote in the introduction to a fellow economist’s book: “[Economics] is a method rather than a doctrine, an apparatus of the mind, a technique of thinking, which helps its possessor to draw correct conclusions.” In other words, economics teaches you how to think, not what to think.
p106.zh: 20世纪最伟大的经济学家之一约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯(1883–1946)指出,经济学不仅仅是一个主题领域,也是一种思维方式. 凯恩斯(Keynes)在对经济学家同行的著作的介绍中写道 : “ 经济学是一种方法,而不是一种理论,一种思想机器,一种思维技巧,帮助拥有者得出正确的结论。 ”换句话说,经济学教你如何思考,而不是怎样思考。

p107.original: Watch this video about John Maynard Keynes and his influence on economics.
p107.zh: 看这段关于约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯的视频以及他对经济学的影响.

p108.original: Economists see the world through a different lens than anthropologists, biologists, classicists, or practitioners of any other discipline.  They analyze issues and problems using economic theories that are based on particular assumptions about human behavior. These assumptions tend to be different than the assumptions an anthropologist or psychologist might use. A theory is a simplified representation of how two or more variables interact with each other.   The purpose of a theory is to take a complex, real-world issue and simplify it down to its essentials. If done well, this enables the analyst to understand the issue and any problems around it. A good theory is simple enough to understand, while complex enough to capture the key features of the object or situation you are studying.
p108.zh: 经济学家通过不同于人类学家,生物学家,经典学家,或任何其他学科的从业者的角度看待世界. 他们利用基于对人类行为的特定假设的经济理论来分析问题和问题. 这些假设往往不同于人类学家或心理学家可能采用的假设. 一个理论是两个或两个以上变量如何相互作用的简化表述. 一个理论的目的是把一个复杂的,现实世界的问题,简化到它的本质. 如果做得好,则使分析师能够了解问题及其周围的任何问题。 一个好的理论是足够简单的来理解的,而复杂的理论足以捕捉你正在研究的对象或情况的关键特征.

p109.original: Sometimes economists use the term model instead of theory.  Strictly speaking, a theory is a more abstract representation, while a model is a more applied or empirical representation.  We use models to test theories, but for this course we will use the terms interchangeably.
p109.zh: 有时经济学家会使用模型一词而不是理论.严格地说,一个理论是一种比较抽象的表述,而模型是一种比较应用或经验性的表现. 我们用模型来测试理论, 但是对于这个课程,我们将交替使用术语。

p110.original: For example, an architect who is planning a major office building will often build a physical model that sits on a tabletop to show how the entire city block will look after the new building is constructed. Companies often build models of their new products, which are more rough and unfinished than the final product, but can still demonstrate how the new product will work.
p110.zh: 例如,正在规划大型办公楼的建筑师往往会建造一个坐落在台顶上的物理模型,以显示整个城市街区将如何照顾新建筑的建造.公司往往会为其新产品建立模型,这些模型比最终产品更粗糙且未完成,但仍能展示新产品将如何运作.

p111.original: A good model to start with in economics is the circular flow diagram (). It pictures the economy as consisting of two groups—households and firms—that interact in two markets: the goods and services market in which firms sell and households buy and the labor market in which households sell labor to business firms or other employees.
p111.zh: 在经济学中开始的一个良好模型是循环流图(. 它将经济描绘成两个群体——家庭和公司——在两个市场上相互作用:公司出售的货物和服务市场和家庭购买的货物和服务市场,以及家庭向商业公司或其他雇员出售劳动力的劳工市场。

p113.original: Firms produce and sell goods and services to households in the market for goods and services (or product market).  Arrow “A” indicates this.  Households pay for goods and services, which becomes the revenues to firms.  Arrow “B” indicates this.  Arrows A and B represent the two sides of the product market.  Where do households obtain the income to buy goods and services? They provide the labor and other resources (e.g., land, capital, raw materials) firms need to produce goods and services in the market for inputs (or factors of production).  Arrow “C” indicates this.  In return, firms pay for the inputs (or resources) they use in the form of wages and other factor payments.  Arrow “D” indicates this.  Arrows “C” and “D” represent the two sides of the factor market.
p113.zh: 企业向商品和服务市场(或产品市场)中的住户生产和销售商品和服务。箭头“A”表示这一点。家庭为货物和服务付费,这些货物和服务成为企业的收入。箭头“B”表示这一点。箭头A和B代表产品市场的两面.家庭从哪里获得购买货物和服务的收入? 它们提供劳动力和其他资源(例如土地、资本、原材料),公司需要在市场上生产商品和服务,以获得投入(或生产要素)。箭头“C”表示这一点。 作为回报,公司以工资和其他要素付款的形式支付它们使用的投入(或资源)。箭头“D”表示这一点。箭头“C”和“D”代表要素市场的两面。

p114.original: Of course, in the real world, there are many different markets for goods and services and markets for many different types of labor. The circular flow diagram simplifies this to make the picture easier to grasp. In the diagram, firms produce goods and services, which they sell to households in return for revenues. The outer circle shows this, and represents the two sides of the product market (for example, the market for goods and services) in which households demand and firms supply. Households sell their labor as workers to firms in return for wages, salaries, and benefits. The inner circle shows this and represents the two sides of the labor market in which households supply and firms demand.
p114.zh: 当然,在现实世界中,商品和服务市场和许多不同类型劳动力的市场有很多不同的市场.循环流图简化了这一点,使图片更容易被抓住. 在图中,公司生产货物和服务,它们向家庭出售这些货物和服务以换取收入。外圈表明了这一点,代表了家庭需求和公司供应的产品市场(例如货物和服务市场)的两面。家庭将劳动力作为工人出售给企业,以换取工资、薪金和福利。内圈表明了这一点,并代表了家庭供求的劳动力市场的两面。

p115.original: This version of the circular flow model is stripped down to the essentials, but it has enough features to explain how the product and labor markets work in the economy. We could easily add details to this basic model if we wanted to introduce more real-world elements, like financial markets, governments, and interactions with the rest of the globe (imports and exports).
p115.zh: 这一版本的循环流动模式被剥离到基本部分,但它有足够的特征来解释产品和劳动力市场如何在经济中运作。 如果我们想引入更现实世界的要素,比如金融市场、政府以及同全球其他地方(进出口)的互动,我们就可以轻松地为这一基本模式增添细节。

p116.original: Economists carry a set of theories in their heads like a carpenter carries around a toolkit. When they see an economic issue or problem, they go through the theories they know to see if they can find one that fits. Then they use the theory to derive insights about the issue or problem. Economists express theories as diagrams, graphs, or even as mathematical equations. (Do not worry. In this course, we will mostly use graphs.) Economists do not figure out the answer to the problem first and then draw the graph to illustrate. Rather, they use the graph of the theory to help them figure out the answer. Although at the introductory level, you can sometimes figure out the right answer without applying a model, if you keep studying economics, before too long you will run into issues and problems that you will need to graph to solve. We explain both micro and macroeconomics in terms of theories and models. The most well-known theories are probably those of supply and demand, but you will learn a number of others.
p116.zh: 经济学家在脑中携带着一套理论,就像木匠携带一个工具箱一样. 当他们看到一个经济问题或问题时,他们会通过他们知道的各种理论,看看他们是否能找到一个适合的理论. 然后他们利用理论来获得对问题或问题的见解.经济学家将理论表达为图,图,甚至以数学方程.(别担心。 在此过程中,我们将主要使用图表. )经济学家不会首先找出问题的答案,然后绘制图表来说明. 相反,他们利用理论的图来帮助他们找出答案. 虽然在入门阶段,但有时可以不应用模型而找出正确的答案,如果你继续学习经济学,那么在太长的时间之前,你会遇到你需要用图表来解答的问题和问题. 我们从理论和模型的角度来解释微观和宏观经济。 最知名的理论可能是供求理论,但你们会学到一些其他理论.

p118.original: Economists analyze problems differently than do other disciplinary experts. The main tools economists use are economic theories or models. A theory is not an illustration of the answer to a problem. Rather, a theory is a tool for determining the answer.
p118.zh: 经济学家分析问题的方法与其他学科专家不同.经济学家使用的主要工具是经济理论或模型. 一个理论不是解决问题的答案。 相反,一个理论是确定答案的工具。

p120.original: Suppose we extend the circular flow model to add imports and exports. Copy the circular flow diagram onto a sheet of paper and then add a foreign country as a third agent. Draw a rough sketch of the flows of imports, exports, and the payments for each on your diagram.
p120.zh: 假设我们扩大循环流动模式,增加进出口。将循环流图复制到一张纸上,然后添加一个外国作为第三代理。绘制您图表上的进口、出口流动和每笔付款的粗略示意图。

p121.original: Draw a box outside the original circular flow to represent the foreign country. Draw an arrow from the foreign country to firms, to represents imports. Draw an arrow in the reverse direction representing payments for imports. Draw an arrow from firms to the foreign country to represent exports. Draw an arrow in the reverse direction to represent payments for imports.
p121.zh: 在原循环流外画一个框,代表外国. 从外国向公司划箭,代表进口。向反方向绘制一个箭头,表示对进口的付款。 从企业向外国划箭,代表出口.向反方向绘制箭头,以表示对进口的付款。

p122.original: What is an example of a problem in the world today, not mentioned in the chapter, that has an economic dimension?
p122.zh: 本章没有提到的今天世界上一个具有经济层面的问题的例子是什么?

p123.original: There are many such problems. Consider the AIDS epidemic. Why are so few AIDS patients in Africa and Southeast Asia treated with the same drugs that are effective in the United States and Europe? It is because neither those patients nor the countries in which they live have the resources to purchase the same drugs.
p123.zh: 有许多这样的问题。考虑艾滋病流行病。 为什么非洲和东南亚的艾滋病患者很少使用在美国和欧洲有效的同样药物治疗?这是因为这些病人和他们居住的国家都没有购买同样药物的资源。

p125.original: How did John Maynard Keynes define economics?
p125.zh: 约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯是如何定义经济学的?

p126.original: Are households primarily buyers or sellers in the goods and services market? In the labor market?
p126.zh: 家庭是货物和服务市场上的主要买卖者吗? 在劳动力市场上?

p127.original: Are firms primarily buyers or sellers in the goods and services market? In the labor market?
p127.zh: 公司是货物和服务市场上的主要买家还是卖家? 在劳动力市场上?

p129.original: Why is it unfair or meaningless to criticize a theory as “unrealistic?”
p129.zh: 为什么批评一个理论是“不现实的”是不公平的或毫无意义的?

p130.original: Suppose, as an economist, you are asked to analyze an issue unlike anything you have ever done before. Also, suppose you do not have a specific model for analyzing that issue. What should you do? Hint:  What would a carpenter do in a similar situation?
p130.zh: 假设,作为一个经济学家, 你被要求分析一个问题 与你以前做过的任何事情不同。 而且,假设你没有分析这个问题的具体模式。 你该怎么办?提示:木匠在类似情况下会做什么?.

p131.original: How To Organize Economies: An Overview of Economic Systems
p131.zh: 如何组织经济:经济体系概览

p132.original: Think about what a complex system a modern economy is. It includes all production of goods and services, all buying and selling, all employment. The economic life of every individual is interrelated, at least to a small extent, with the economic lives of thousands or even millions of other individuals. Who organizes and coordinates this system? Who ensures that, for example, the number of televisions a society provides is the same as the amount it needs and wants? Who ensures that the right number of employees work in the electronics industry? Who ensures that televisions are produced in the best way possible? How does it all get done?
p132.zh: 想想现代经济是个什么样的复杂体系. 它包括所有货物和服务的生产、所有买卖、所有就业。每个人的经济生活与成千上万甚至数百万其他个人的经济生活相互关联,至少在一小部分。由谁组织和协调这个系统? 例如,谁能确保一个社会提供的电视数量与其需要和想要的数量相同?由谁确保适当数量的员工在电子行业工作? 谁能确保以尽可能好的方式制作电视?这一切是怎么完成的?

p133.original: There are at least three ways that societies organize an economy. The first is the traditional economy, which is the oldest economic system and is used in parts of Asia, Africa, and South America. Traditional economies organize their economic affairs the way they have always done (i.e., tradition). Occupations stay in the family. Most families are farmers who grow the crops using traditional methods. What you produce is what you consume. Because tradition drives the way of life, there is little economic progress or development.
p133.zh: 社会组织经济至少有三种方式。 第一个是传统经济,它是历史最悠久的经济体系,在亚洲、非洲和南美洲部分地区使用。传统经济按其一贯的做法(即传统)安排其经济事务。职业留在家庭中。 大多数家庭是农民,他们使用传统方法种植作物。 你生产的东西就是消耗的东西。 由于传统驱动着生活方式,经济进步或发展也很少.

p135.original: Command economies are very different. In a command economy, economic effort is devoted to goals passed down from a ruler or ruling class. Ancient Egypt was a good example: a large part of economic life was devoted to building pyramids, like those in , for the pharaohs. Medieval manor life is another example: the lord provided the land for growing crops and protection in the event of war. In return, vassals provided labor and soldiers to do the lord’s bidding. In the last century, communism emphasized command economies.
p135.zh: 指挥经济大相径庭. 在指挥经济中,经济努力致力于从统治者或统治阶级传承下来的目标.古埃及是一个很好的例子:经济生活的很大一部分是用来建造金字塔的,像那些在......的,为法老们建造的金字塔。中世纪的庄园生活是另一个例子:领主提供了土地,用于在战争时种植作物和保护. 作为回报,巫师们提供劳动力和士兵来完成领主的授意. 在上个世纪,共产主义强调指挥经济.

p136.original: In a command economy, the government decides what goods and services will be produced and what prices it will charge for them. The government decides what methods of production to use and sets wages for workers. The government provides many necessities like healthcare and education for free. Currently, Cuba and North Korea have command economies.
p136.zh: 在指挥经济中,政府决定将生产哪些货物和服务,以及收取哪些价格。 政府决定使用何种生产方法,并确定工人的工资。 政府免费提供保健和教育等许多必需品。 目前,古巴和朝鲜实行统帅经济.

p138.original: Although command economies have a very centralized structure for economic decisions, market economies have a very decentralized structure. A market is an institution that brings together buyers and sellers of goods or services, who may be either individuals or businesses. The New York Stock Exchange () is a prime example of a market which brings buyers and sellers together. In a market economy, decision-making is decentralized. Market economies are based on private enterprise: the private individuals or groups of private individuals own and operate the means of production (resources and businesses). Businesses supply goods and services based on demand. (In a command economy, by contrast, the government owns resources and businesses.) Supply of goods and services depends on what the demands are. A person’s income is based on their ability to convert resources (especially labor) into something that society values. The more society values the person’s output, the higher the income (think Lady Gaga or LeBron James).  In this scenario, market forces, not governments, determine economic decisions.
p138.zh: 虽然指令性经济体的经济决策结构非常集中,但市场经济的结构却非常分散。市场是将货物或服务的买卖双方聚集在一起的机构,他们可以是个人或企业。纽约证券交易所()是将买方和卖方聚集在一起的市场的主要例子。 在市场经济中,决策是分散的。市场经济以私营企业为基础:私人个人或个人团体拥有并经营生产资料(资源和企业)。企业根据需求提供商品和服务.(在指挥经济中,相反,政府拥有资源和企业。 )货物和服务的供应取决于需求是什么。个人的收入取决于他们能否将资源(特别是劳动力)转化为社会珍视的东西。社会越重视个人产出,收入就越高(认为Lady Gaga或LeBron James). 在这种情况下,由市场力量而不是政府决定经济决策。

p139.original: Most economies in the real world are mixed. They combine elements of command and market (and even traditional) systems. The U.S. economy is positioned toward the market-oriented end of the spectrum. Many countries in Europe and Latin America, while primarily market-oriented, have a greater degree of government involvement in economic decisions than the U.S. economy. China and Russia, while over the past several decades have moved more in the direction of having a market-oriented system, remain closer to the command economy end of the spectrum. The Heritage Foundation provides  perspective on countries’ economic freedom, as the following Clear It Up feature discusses.
p139.zh: 现实世界的大多数经济体情况喜忧参半。 它们结合了指挥和市场(甚至传统)系统的要素. 美国经济正朝着面向市场的方向发展。 欧洲和拉丁美洲的许多国家虽然主要面向市场,但政府参与经济决策的程度比美国经济要大. 中国和俄罗斯虽然在过去几十年中朝着建立面向市场体系的方向迈出了更多的步伐,但仍更接近于指令性经济的尽头。传统基金会提供各国经济自由的视角,

p140.original: What countries are considered economically free?
p140.zh: 哪些国家被视为经济自由的国家?

p141.original: Who is in control of economic decisions? Are people free to do what they want and to work where they want? Are businesses free to produce when they want and what they choose, and to hire and fire as they wish? Are banks free to choose who will receive loans, or does the government control these kinds of choices? Each year, researchers at the Heritage Foundation and the Wall Street Journal look at 50 different categories of economic freedom for countries around the world. They give each nation a score based on the extent of economic freedom in each category. Note that while the Heritage Foundation/WSJ index is widely cited by an array of scholars and publications, it should be regarded as only one viewpoint. Some experts indicate that the index’s category choices and scores are politically biased. However, the index and others like it provide a useful resource for critical discussion of economic freedom.
p141.zh: 谁控制着经济决策? 人们是否可以自由地做他们想做的事,并且可以去他们想要的地方工作?企业是否可以随意生产,选择什么,雇佣和开火?银行是可以自由选择谁将获得贷款,还是政府控制了这些选择? 每年,遗产基金会和华尔街日报的研究人员都会研究世界各国的50个不同类别的经济自由. 它们根据每一类国家的经济自由程度给每个国家打分。请注意,尽管遗产基金会/WSJ指数被众多学者和出版物广泛引用,但应当将其视为一种观点。 一些专家表示,该指数的类别选择和分数具有政治偏见. 然而,该指数和其他类似指数为批评经济自由的讨论提供了有用的资源。

p142.original: The 2016 Heritage Foundation’s Index of Economic Freedom report ranked 178 countries around the world:  lists some examples of the most free and the least free countries. Although technically not a separate country, Hong Kong has been granted a degree of autonomy such that, for purposes of measuring economic statistics, it is often treated as a separate country. Several additional countries were not ranked because of extreme instability that made judgments about economic freedom impossible. These countries include Afghanistan, Iraq, Libya, Syria, Somalia, and Yemen.
p142.zh: 2016年遗产基金会经济自由指数报告排名全球178个国家:列出一些最自由,最不自由的国家的例子. 虽然在技术上不是一个单独的国家,但香港已获得一定程度的自治权,因此,为了衡量经济统计的目的,它往往被视为一个单独的国家。另有几个国家没有排名,因为极端不稳定,无法对经济自由作出判断。这些国家包括阿富汗、伊拉克、利比亚、叙利亚、索马里和也门。

p143.original: The assigned rankings are inevitably based on estimates, yet even these rough measures can be useful for discerning trends. In 2015, 101 of the 178 included countries shifted toward greater economic freedom, although 77 of the countries shifted toward less economic freedom. In recent decades, the overall trend has been a higher level of economic freedom around the world.
p143.zh: 所分配的排名不可避免地是基于估计,然而,即使这些粗略的衡量方法也可用于辨别趋势。2015年,178个国家中有101个国家转向更大的经济自由,尽管77个国家转向较少的经济自由。近几十年来,全世界总的趋势是经济自由水平更高。

p171.original: Regulations: The Rules of the Game

p172.original: Markets and government regulations are always entangled. There is no such thing as an absolutely free market. Regulations always define the “rules of the game” in the economy. Economies that are primarily market-oriented have fewer regulations—ideally just enough to maintain an even playing field for participants. At a minimum, these laws govern matters like safeguarding private property against theft, protecting people from violence, enforcing legal contracts, preventing fraud, and collecting taxes. Conversely, even the most command-oriented economies operate using markets. How else would buying and selling occur? The government heavily regulates decisions of what to produce and prices to charge. Heavily regulated economies often have underground economies (or black markets), which are markets where the buyers and sellers make transactions without the government’s approval.
p172.zh: 市场和政府规章总是纠缠在一起。绝对自由市场是不存在的。条例总是界定经济中的“游戏规则”。主要是面向市场的经济体的监管较少,最理想的就是保持参与者的公平竞争环境。这些法律至少管辖保护私人财产免遭盗窃、保护人民免遭暴力、执行法律合同、防止欺诈和征税等事项。 相反,即使是最以指挥为主的经济体也利用市场运作。 否则买卖会怎样发生?政府对生产产品和收费价格的决定进行严格管制。受严格监管的经济体往往拥有地下经济(或黑市),而黑市是买卖双方未经政府批准进行交易的市场。

p173.original: The question of how to organize economic institutions is typically not a straightforward choice between all market or all government, but instead involves a balancing act over the appropriate combination of market freedom and government rules.
p173.zh: 如何组织经济机构的问题通常不是所有市场或所有政府之间的直接选择,而是涉及平衡行为,而不是将市场自由和政府规则适当结合起来。

p176.original: Recent decades have seen a trend toward globalization, which is the expanding cultural, political, and economic connections between people around the world. One measure of this is the increased buying and selling of goods, services, and assets across national borders—in other words, international trade and financial capital flows.
p176.zh: 最近几十年出现了全球化的趋势,即世界各地人民之间的文化、政治和经济联系不断扩大。 其中一项措施是,跨界货物、服务和资产的买卖增加,换句话说,是国际贸易和金融资本流动。

p177.original: Globalization has occurred for a number of reasons. Improvements in shipping, as illustrated by the container ship in , and air cargo have driven down transportation costs. Innovations in computing and telecommunications have made it easier and cheaper to manage long-distance economic connections of production and sales. Many valuable products and services in the modern economy can take the form of information—for example: computer software; financial advice; travel planning; music, books and movies; and blueprints for designing a building. These products and many others can be transported over telephones and computer networks at ever-lower costs. Finally, international agreements and treaties between countries have encouraged greater trade.
p177.zh: 全球化的出现有若干原因。运输的改善,例如集装箱船在......,以及航空货物使运输费用下降。计算和电信方面的创新使得管理生产和销售的长途经济联系更加容易和便宜。现代经济中许多有价值的产品和服务可以采取信息的形式——例如:计算机软件;财务咨询;旅行规划;音乐、书籍和电影;以及设计建筑物的蓝图。 这些产品和其他许多产品可以通过电话和计算机网络以越来越低的成本运输。 最后,国际协议和国家间条约鼓励了更大的贸易。

p178.original: presents one measure of globalization. It shows the percentage of domestic economic production that was exported for a selection of countries from 2010 to 2015, according to an entity known as The World Bank. Exports are the goods and services that one produces domestically and sells abroad. Imports are the goods and services that one produces abroad and then sells domestically. Gross domestic product (GDP) measures the size of total production in an economy. Thus, the ratio of exports divided by GDP measures what share of a country’s total economic production is sold in other countries.
p178.zh: 提出了全球化的一个尺度。 它显示2010年至2015年为一些国家出口的国内经济生产的百分比,据一个称为世界银行的实体称。出口是在国内生产和在国外销售的货物和服务。进口是在国外生产、然后在国内销售的货物和服务。国内生产总值(GDP)衡量一个经济体的总生产规模。 因此,按国内总产值计算,出口比率除以一国经济总产量中有多少份额在其他国家销售。

p179.zh: 全球化的程度(出口/国内生产总值)

p267.original: In recent decades, the export/GDP ratio has generally risen, both worldwide and for the U.S. economy. Interestingly, the share of U.S. exports in proportion to the U.S. economy is well below the global average, in part because large economies like the United States can contain more of the division of labor inside their national borders. However, smaller economies like Belgium, Korea, and Canada need to trade across their borders with other countries to take full advantage of division of labor, specialization, and economies of scale. In this sense, the enormous U.S. economy is less affected by globalization than most other countries.
p267.zh: 近几十年来,出口/国内生产总值比率普遍上升,无论是在世界范围内还是对于美国经济而言。有趣的是,美国出口占美国经济的比例远低于全球平均水平,部分原因是美国这样的大经济体可以控制更多国内的劳动分工. 然而,像比利时、韩国和加拿大这样的较小经济体需要与其他国家进行跨界贸易,以充分利用劳动分工、专业化和规模经济。 在这个意义上,巨大的美国经济受到全球化的影响比大多数其他国家要小.

p268.original: indicates that many medium and low income countries around the world, like Mexico and China, have also experienced a surge of globalization in recent decades. If an astronaut in orbit could put on special glasses that make all economic transactions visible as brightly colored lines and look down at Earth, the astronaut would see the planet covered with connections.
p268.zh: 这表明,近几十年来,世界各地许多中低收入国家,如墨西哥和中国,也经历了全球化的猛增。 如果在轨宇航员可以戴上特别的眼镜,使所有经济交易都以明亮的彩色线条可见并俯视地球,宇航员就会看到这个星球上覆盖着各种连接.

p269.original: Despite the rise in globalization over the last few decades, in recent years we've seen significant pushback against globalization from people across the world concerned about loss of jobs, loss of political sovereignty, and increased economic inequality. Prominent examples of this pushback include the 2016 vote in Great Britain to exit the European Union (i.e. Brexit), and the election of Donald J. Trump for President of the United States.
p269.zh: 尽管全球化在过去几十年中有所上升,但近年来我们看到全世界人民对全球化的强烈反弹,他们担心失业、政治主权的丧失和经济不平等加剧。 这种推倒的突出例子包括2016年大不列颠投票退出欧盟(即.Brexit),以及唐纳德·J·马赛尔(Donald J.特朗普为美国总统.

p271.original: Information Overload in the Information Age

p272.original: The world provides nearly instant access to a wealth of information. Consider that as recently as the late 1970s, the Farmer’s Almanac, along with the Weather Bureau of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, were the primary sources American farmers used to determine when to plant and harvest their crops. Today, these decisions are driven by data. Farmers access detailed data streams driven by global positioning systems, historical rainfall patterns, and complex weather monitoring services. They combine this information with crop yield data and soil quality measurements from prior years. Maximizing production efficiently can mean the difference between a farm that remains profitable and one that may need to sell its land, and data helps eliminate guesswork.
p272.zh: 世界几乎可以立即获得大量信息。想想最近到20世纪70年代末, 农民的Almanac, 以及美国的气象局。农业部是美国农民用来决定何时种植和收获作物的主要来源。 今天,这些决定是由数据驱动的。农民获得由全球定位系统、历史降雨模式和复杂的天气监测服务驱动的详细数据流。 它们将这一信息与作物产量数据和前几年的土壤质量测量结合起来。高效实现生产最大化,可以指保持盈利的农场和可能需要出售其土地的农场之间的区别,数据有助于消除猜测。

p273.original: Information helps us make decisions as simple as what to wear today to how many reporters the media should send to cover an event. Each of these decisions is an economic decision. After all, resources are scarce. If the media send ten reporters to cover an announcement, they are not available to cover other stories or complete other tasks. Information provides the necessary knowledge to make the best possible decisions on how to utilize scarce resources. Welcome to the world of economics!
p273.zh: 资讯有助于我们做出与今天穿什么一样简单的决定,每一项决定都是经济决定。毕竟,资源稀缺。 如果媒体派10名记者报道某项公告,他们无法报道其他报道或完成其他任务。信息提供了必要的知识,可以就如何利用稀缺资源作出尽可能好的决定。 欢迎来到经济学的世界!

p275.original: We can organize societies as traditional, command, or market-oriented economies. Most societies are a mix. The last few decades have seen globalization evolve as a result of growth in commercial and financial networks that cross national borders, making businesses and workers from different economies increasingly interdependent.
p275.zh: 我们可以把社会组织成传统、指挥或面向市场的经济。 大多数社会都是混合的。 过去几十年里,全球化由于跨越国界的商业和金融网络的增长而演变,使来自不同经济体的企业和工人日益相互依存。

p277.original: The chapter defines private enterprise as a characteristic of market-oriented economies. What would public enterprise be? Hint: It is a characteristic of command economies.

p278.original: Public enterprise means the factors of production (resources and businesses) are owned and operated by the government.
p278.zh: 公有企业是指生产要素(资源和企业)为政府所有和经营.

p279.original: Why might Belgium, France, Italy, and Sweden have a higher export to GDP ratio than the United States?
p279.zh: 为什么比利时,法国,意大利,瑞典的出口与GDP的比率会比美国高?.

p280.original: The United States is a large country economically speaking, so it has less need to trade internationally than the other countries mentioned. (This is the same reason that France and Italy have lower ratios than Belgium or Sweden.) One additional reason is that each of the other countries is a member of the European Union, where trade between members occurs without barriers to trade, like tariffs and quotas.
p280.zh: 从经济上讲,美国是一个大国,因此它比提到的其他国家更不需要进行国际贸易。(这也是法国和意大利比率低于比利时或瑞典的原因. )另一个原因是,其他国家都是欧洲联盟成员国,成员国之间的贸易没有贸易壁垒,如关税和配额。
